title: Family music and radio and records in childhood
summary: Toussaint talks about his father's trumpet, his sister and brother playing, and how radio mattered more than scarce records.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: But my father didn't play trumpet for a while. Barely, they never did any real popularity, but he did play trumpet. Not above living, he didn't play enough to support himself or things like that. But for a while it was in the early part of his life, I think later on he had to raise a family. He did that. My sister played the piano. My brother played guitar. And so, my mother, the radio and I.
Do you have records at home too? Have phonograph records at home too?

Do I have or did I? Did you then in those days? Well, ever now and then, now, the record would come by. Not that it was during depression, but I still remember that there were graphing over in the neighborhood. And records weren't really plentiful at all. They were very thick, seven eggs. And a few people in the neighborhood had a new-fangled record player. But most of it was radio, more than record.
Well, those were the days of Ernie the Whip.
Well, I remember even though before, like in my early childhood, five, six, seven, eight.
Were there local stations and local people recording in your childhood? Do you remember?

Well, I remember the music more than well aware they were recorded. I remember things like that. That was no concern. But whatever was on the ready was something you were supposed to play on the piano for a lot of concern. Even if you were a national anthem.
